item.title: Observation of a thermite reaction
item.description: A standard thermite reaction (typically composed of aluminum powder and iron oxide) burns at temperatures up to 2,500 °C (4,532 °F). Depending on the specific mixture and how quickly heat escapes into the surrounding area, the reaction front can range anywhere between 2,200 °C and 2,800 °C (4,000 °F to 5,000 °F). To put this extreme heat into perspective: • Twice as hot as lava: Volcanic lava generally flows at around 700 °C to 1,200 °C, meaning thermite is more than double its temperature. • Easily melts steel: Steel has a melting point of roughly 1,510 °C (2,750 °F), allowing thermite to liquefy steel structures and engine blocks in seconds. • Half the temperature of the sun: The surface of the sun rests at about 5,500 °C, making a thermite fire nearly half as hot

item.title: Corporate America worships Buffett as the Oracle of fucking Omaha, right up until he says they should pay their goddamn taxes.
item.description:
Notice the pattern, because it’s about as subtle as a brick through a window. When Buffett picks stocks, he’s the Oracle of fucking Omaha, and the business press treats every mumble like scripture. When he suggests that the most profitable institutions on earth might hand over a share of their profits, like the rest of society manages to, suddenly he’s a nice old man who’s lost the plot.
This isn’t hypocrisy by accident. It’s the system working exactly as designed. Wisdom is whatever makes the powerful richer, and everything else is “naive,” “unrealistic,” or, God help us, “class warfare.” The same crowd that spends decades lobbying for loopholes then acts shocked, shocked, when someone from their own club says the quiet part out loud. And let’s not pretend this is abstract. Berkshire reportedly sent Washington over $5 billion in federal taxes in a single year, and Buffett’s attitude was basically “it doesn’t bother me.” Meanwhile dozens of enormously profitable corporations pay nothing in federal income tax in a given year, through accelerated depreciation, credits, and stock-option deductions. All perfectly legal, of course, because the people who benefit wrote the fucking rules. Then the same people lecture a nurse about “personal responsibility.” The arithmetic of the original claim is back-of-the-envelope and people argue about it. That’s not the point. The point is the sweat on that poor bastard’s forehead: the sudden, desperate realization that the man they’ve been quoting for sixty years has just said something inconvenient. item.title: GovBrief Today #646
item.description: A federal judge wants to know whether Donald Trump's Justice Department lied to her about the public golf course he plans to rebuild. Government lawyers told Judge Ana Reyes for months that the plans for East Potomac Golf Course weren't final, even as Trump posted that they were and workers cut down at least 400 trees. "Rarely, if ever, has the United States Department of Justice urged a federal court not to believe the sitting president," she wrote. "For months, the court trusted, but did not verify," Reyes said last week. "No longer." Today she announced plans to name a special master, an outside investigator answering to the court, to learn whether officials and their lawyers misled her. Her pick is Jessie Liu, Trump's own US attorney for Washington during his first term. I've emailed 9,845 stories over 646 straight nights, free and without ads.
